Serial precondition from triage is **satisfied**: **PR #11470** (cards #11096 + #11097) is **merged**, so the batched `$in` read, the equality-gated writes, `seed-name-lookup.ts`'s `buildExistingByName`, and the `bootstrap-seed-round-trips.test.ts` pins are all on `main`. The dev branches from a tree containing the shape it is asked to extend.

Dispatch fences carried to the dev:
- The card names three design options and says the choice **should be made deliberately, not inside another card's PR**. That choice is in scope for this card — but it must be **written down before the code**, with the reason, and the PR must state which option was taken and why the other two were not.
- ⛔ Option 2 widens `seed-name-lookup.ts`, which **three seeders now depend on**. If option 2 is chosen, every existing caller must be shown unaffected by measurement, not by inspection — and the `#8470` narrowing (the platform's own organization-less row) must be shown still load-bearing, not merely still present.
- ⛔ **Do not move or relax any round-trip pin** to make a number fit. `bootstrap-seed-round-trips.test.ts` is the ratchet; a pin that has to move is a finding to report, not a line to edit.
- ⛔ No `packages/spec/**` edits.
- The card is explicit that **the slope of this axis has not been measured** and that the hosted rig lives in `objectstack-ai/cloud`. Do not claim a measured speedup. The defensible claim is the round-trip count, pinned in-repo — nothing more.

## Curated half **merged** (PR #11537). Card stays open for the derived half → `pm:blocked`, `Blocked-by: #11520`.

Assignee cleared; `pm:dispatched` → `pm:blocked`. The PR was deliberately `Part of`, not `Fixes`, so nothing auto-closed this — correct, because the card's scope is not finished.

### What landed

Option **2's mechanism at option 3's scope**: `seed-name-lookup.ts` gained an optional equality predicate carried alongside the `$in`, applied to the **curated half only**; the reconcile is equality-gated for **both** halves.

The dev reframed the card's own options before choosing, and the reframing is right: the three options conflate *how* to batch a predicated read (1 vs 2) with *which halves* to batch (3). Option 1 was rejected on measured grounds, not preference — it returns the **wrong row** (#8470 exactly), it **truncates**, and it would not even have avoided widening the shared file.

Verified from the merge base rather than from the report:
- `bootstrap-seed-round-trips.test.ts` — **zero removed lines**, additions only ⇒ no pre-existing round-trip pin moved, which was the fence I set
- **zero** `packages/spec/**`, `content/docs/releases/**`, or governed-surface edits
- the shared-file widening is opt-in: `...(equals ?? {})` spreads nothing when absent, so the three existing callers emit the identical key set — and the PR closes the `undefined`-key loophole with an explicit `Object.keys(…)` pin rather than trusting `toEqual`, which would have accepted either

⭐ Two things worth keeping visible on this card:
- **The predicate rides the degradation read too.** `perItemIndex` — the no-`$in` fallback — takes and applies it, because *"a fallback that dropped it would ask a WIDER question than the batched read it is standing in for; for the caller that needs one, wider is not 'slower but the same': it is a different row."*
- **The precondition is stated and assigned to the caller**, with the reason it cannot backfire: *"Narrowing can only SHRINK a page, so passing a predicate never makes truncation likelier than the unpredicated read it replaces."* ⇒ this change **cannot** make #11518 worse.

### What remains, and why it is blocked rather than queued

The **derived half** is still per-item, and that is a decision, not leftover work. Its lookup is cross-organization by construction, and `derivedRowIsOurs` / `skippedAuthored` / #8751's `platformStampedInOrg` are all computed from the lowest-`id` row installation-wide. Narrowing it stops counting a real anomaly and starts seeding the bucket in the case **#8552 ruled must be left alone**; batching it unnarrowed needs an unbounded read.

**#11520** carries the full analysis and three options (A: truncation-detecting batched read · B: bucket-scoped · C: leave per-item), so the next attempt does not re-derive them. It is `finding` and awaiting triage grading — hence `pm:blocked` here rather than back to `pm:queue`.

⚠️ The dev's own note on option B, worth not losing: it **should not be taken quietly — it reverses part of #8552 by way of a read shape.**

Also recorded: on a **stock** installation the derived set is **empty** (the platform's own permission sets grant only names already in `KNOWN_CAPABILITIES`; package-declared names are excluded via `materializedCapabilityNames`). It grows only for an app whose `defaultPermissionSets` grant capability strings nothing declares. So C is defensible on its own until #11518 is being repaired anyway.

### Not measured — do not let the merge imply otherwise

**No speedup and no slope.** The hosted `bootstrap-curve.mjs` rig lives in `objectstack-ai/cloud` on different axes. The only claims this PR makes are the round-trip **count** and the **identity** of the rows each leg touches, both pinned in-repo. Real-driver behaviour is also unmeasured — every number came from in-memory doubles.

Refs: PR #11537 (merged) · **#11520** (the derived half, blocking this card) · #11518 (the unscoped page-cap defect this work uncovered, live on `main`) · #8470 / #8552 / #8751 / #10946 / #11096
